newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho shrugs shoulders at EU/Anglo news.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho shrugs shoulders at EU/Anglo news.

text.p: Lonrho Plc shrugged its shoulders at news its biggest shareholder, Anglo American Corp, had offered to trim its 28.4 percent stake in the British conglomerate to appease the EU.
The size of Anglo's holding would have no bearing on Lonrho's long-stated plan to break itself up, a company spokesman said on Friday.
"It will have no effect on Lonrho's plans whatsoever," he said, declining further comment.
Sources close to Anglo earlier said the South African firm would cut its stake to less than 10 percent to allay fears it and Lonrho would form one front and dominate world platinum markets.
These fears had prompted the European Commission to launch an investigation late last year after Anglo boosted its Lonrho holding to its current level.
The Commission has until May 5 to decide whether to approve Anglo's holding, but sources told Reuters it was most likely to announce its findings on Wednesday already.
Anglo's interest in Lonrho was aroused last year when the British company said it would streamline its businesses by seperating its hotels, African trading and mining operations.
Anglo was particularly interested in the mining business where it saw scope for some sort of co-operation in gold production.
But it was the possibility of a close combination of the platinum activities which raised concerns with Europe's competition authorities.
Early in 1996, the European Commission blocked a planned merger between the platinum operations of Lonrho and Anglo's South African's rival Gencor Ltd.
Anglo, Gencor and Lonrho together are good for about 60 procent of the world's platinum output. The precious metal is used in car exhaust catalysts.
Lonrho shares were unchanged at 135 pence in late afternoon trade.
